title: Triage quickstart canvas + incident playbook (mini-wires)
content:
Goal: Create a compact, actionable "quickstart" triage canvas embedded in the Console's error inspector. Primary target: engineers who need to diagnose and recover from transient timeouts, 5xx responses, and model-generated errors with minimal context switching.

Problem statement:
- Customers and SREs repeatedly open long traces and hit cognitive overload for the most common error classes (request timeouts, 5xx infra errors, model runtime exceptions).
- Current Investigator/Inspector pages are powerful but dense; new on-call hires and product engineers ask for a ‘guided’ flow that suggests most-likely causes and next steps.

Design principles (short):
- Lightweight: one-pane summary + 2 contextual drill panels.
- Prescriptive: show top 3 likely root causes with one-click actions (retry, reroute, rollback model, increase timeout).
- Telemetry-first: surface the minimal signals that change decisions (latency distribution, failure rate delta, model logs snippet).
- Safe defaults: any corrective action requires confirmation and shows estimated impact.
- Non-blocking: keep the main request timeline intact; canvas overlays it rather than replacing.

Persona and scenario examples:
- On-call SRE: returning from pager — wants to know if an edge-region routing issue or GPU OOM caused 5xx spikes.
- Product engineer: single customer reporting hallucination-like model exception — wants quick repro and mapping to model version.
- Platform engineer: capacity autoscaler misfiring — wants to compare queue depth vs. successful throughput.

Mini-wireframe (text sketch):
- Header: short incident summary line (e.g., "5xx spike — us-west-2 — +18% errors in 5m") + quick actions: [Acknowledge] [Annotate] [Create Incident]
- Left column (canvas): compact timeline 15m with error heatmap; colored bands (timeouts, 5xx, model-excs). Hover reveals sample request id.
- Center column (triage card stack): three stacked cards (Likely cause: latency/backpressure / Model runtime exception / Routing fallback). Each card includes: confidence % (derived), top evidence (metric deltas + sample traces), one-click action buttons (Collect trace, Retry with increased timeout, Route to backup model, Escalate to SRE).
- Right column (context drawer): quick facts: recent deploys, config changes, quota alerts, top affected customers (masked), recent logs excerpt (first 4 lines), model version and quantization.
- Footer: recommended next steps checklist + estimated cost and latency impact of each corrective action.

Micro-interactions and behaviours:
- Auto-suggest: the triage stack is seeded by a rules engine (see TODO: rules list). When the inspector opens on an error group, the canvas pre-selects the top card.
- Actions are optimistic: e.g., "Retry with increased timeout" triggers a test reroute for a sample request only; shows result inline and a fast diff of latency vs baseline.
- Snapshots: clicking "Collect trace" captures a short synthetic trace (if possible) and pins it to the incident for later analysis.
- Annotations: every action auto-creates an entry that can be copied into Incident Timeline/Slack.

Evidence signals to display (minimal set):
- Error rate change (5m / 1h baseline) as %
- P50/P95/P99 latencies for the route and model inference time
- Queue depth or batch size histogram (if available)
- Sample error logs (first 3 unique messages)
- Model token-generation abort reasons when available (OOM, token-limit-exceeded, invalid-input)

Backlog grooming (prioritised):
1) RED-OPS-781: Canvas seed rules + schema (MVP) — implement rule set for timeouts / 5xx / model-exc — acceptance: canvas shows correct top cause for synthetic incidents (owner: Rahul).
2) RED-UI-322: Mini-wires implementation — left/canvas/center/right layout responsive down to tablet. ACs: mobile not required for MVP; one-click actions show confirmation modal.
3) RED-API-614: Sample reroute API (test-only flag) — small-scope backend route for non-prod reroutes. AC: reroute succeeds and returns test result within 3s.
4) RED-TELE-203: Telemetry feed for model error enums — add short schema for model runtime failure reasons.
5) RED-SEC-119: Masking rules for top-afflicted-customer list — must redact PII.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Canvas appears on inspector open for error groups with >3 failures in last 15m.
- Shows top-3 triage cards with evidence snippets.
- One-click test-actions (Collect trace, Retry sample, Route sample) work end-to-end in staging.
- Generates an incident timeline entry when any action is executed.
- Unit tests for rules engine and e2e smoke.

Telemetry & success metrics to track post-launch:
- Time-to-first-action for on-call (median) — target: reduce from 8m to 3m.
- Fraction of incidents where canvas suggested correct root cause (sampled human verification) — target 70% for MVP.
- Number of false corrective actions executed (ops safety metric) — target <5% in first month.

Open questions / unresolved tradeoffs (notes to self):
- How opinionated should evidence ranking be vs letting user sort? (default sort by confidence but allow manual reorder).
- Do we allow automatic rollback/rollback-scripts from the canvas? (safety concerns — likely manual only).
- Interaction with Dedicated routing policies — need an RBAC check to avoid non-privileged reroutes.
- Model-errors: sometimes the model error is downstream (prompt bug). We should show matched prompt fingerprints from recent calls to help.

Edge-case flows and fallbacks:
- If the telemetry stream is delayed or missing, show degraded canvas with explicit banner and link to raw trace viewer.
- For long-tail errors (single customer spikes), default canvas to 'investigate customer' mode with a customer-focused checklist.

Prototype notes (visual cues):
- Use compact chips (green/orange/red) for confidence band.
- Each triage card should support expanding to show 5 sample traces inline.
- Keep color legend simple and accessible (avoid red-only signaling).

Meeting notes from sync (2026-03-08):
- Miguel: prefer smaller first iteration, focus on timeouts + 5xx. Model-errors will be second sprint.
- Claire: telemetry schema change needs coordination with serving runtime team (RED-TELE-203).
- Rahul: ops safety gating for reroutes is high priority. Will draft RBAC model.

Next steps / action items (short):
- Rahul: finalize rules list and example incidents (due 2026-03-17).
- Miguel: prototype mini-wires in Figma and link PR (due 2026-03-20).
- Aisha (me): write up developer-facing API contract for test reroutes + annotation format (draft by 2026-03-15).

Rough screenshots to create in Figma (TODO list):
- Canvas overlay with stacked triage cards, small timeline and right drawer.
- Confirmation modal for "Retry with increased timeout" showing estimated latency/cost impact.
- Degraded canvas state when telemetry missing.

Quick UX cheat-sheet for docs page (to carry into help center):
- What it is: a guided troubleshooting canvas embedded in the error inspector for common infra and model failures.
- When to use: first stop after seeing a short-lived spike in errors or timeouts.
- What not to do: do not use for long-running incidents requiring full incident response — use Incident Console.

Notes to self: keep language prescriptive in UI copy ("Check queue depth" vs "You might check queue depth"). We want to reduce hesitation for new on-call engineers.

End of doc.
